post.summary: Generate a new API key for the authenticated user
post.description:
Creates a new API key associated with the currently authenticated user.
The key is only shown once at creation time and cannot be retrieved later,

Authentication is required via JWT token, API key, or Firebase token.
The user ID is extracted from the authentication context.

Parameters:

post.summary: Run a backtest
post.description:
This endpoint runs a single-strategy backtest using `strategy_json`.

ATR parameters (atr_period, atr_volatility_factor) are read from `execution_config`.
If not provided, defaults from trading_defaults.json are used. These values are
injected into the Strategy object at runtime and should NOT be included in strategy_json.

Market data can be sourced from:
- Market Data API: set `data_source="api"` (default) and provide `asset`, `interval`, `lookback_months`
- Local CSV file: set `data_source="file"` and provide `data_file`

Legacy support:
- `hourly_data_file` is accepted and treated as `data_file` (file mode)

Returns:
- success: Boolean indicating if backtest completed successfully
- metrics: Dict with performance metrics
- trade_history: List of serialized TradeRecord objects (entry/exit prices, timestamps, profit/loss, exit reasons)
- error: Error message if backtest failed
- execution_time_seconds: Time taken to run backtest
- trade_count: Number of trades executed
- strategy_names: List of strategy names that were run

post.summary: Run backtests for multiple strategies over a shared date range
post.description:
Market data is fetched once per unique (asset, timeframe) pair and
shared across all strategies that need the same data.  For example,
four BTC/1h strategies result in a single API call for BTC 1h data.

Strategy sources
----------------
Provide exactly one of:
- **strategy_ids** -- list of UUIDs from the strategies table. Strategies
  are loaded from the database and must belong to the caller's org.
- **strategy_configs** -- list of strategy config objects in the canonical
  entry/exit format (same structure as the ``strategy_json`` field in
  ``POST /backtest``, but already parsed as JSON objects, not strings).

Date range
----------
Both ``start_date`` and ``end_date`` are required.

Execution config
----------------
``execution_config`` is optional and is applied to every strategy in the
batch.  Per-strategy execution_config embedded inside each strategy record
is merged on top of this value.  If omitted entirely, defaults from
``trading_defaults.json`` are used (atr_period=14, atr_volatility_factor=2.0).

Failures
--------
Individual strategy failures are captured per-result and do not abort
the batch.  Check ``results[i].success`` and ``results[i].error`` for
each strategy.

Subscription counting
---------------------
Each strategy result with ``trade_count >= 4`` increments the backtest
usage counter once.  The total required quota is checked upfront.

post.summary: Evaluate multiple strategies at the current bar with shared market data
post.description:
Evaluate multiple strategies at the current market bar. Market data is fetched once per unique (asset, timeframe) pair and shared across all strategies that need it, minimizing API calls. Individual strategy failures are captured per-result without aborting the batch. Both strategy_ids and strategy_configs may be provided in the same request.
Supply strategy_ids (DB UUIDs), strategy_configs (inline objects), or both.
Each strategy is evaluated independently at the current price bar; results
include any orders generated (entry, SL, TP) without running a full
historical simulation.

post.summary: Evaluate strategy with current market data
post.description:
Evaluate strategy with current market data and optionally persist results
This endpoint evaluates a strategy against current market conditions:
1. Loads strategy with execution_config and execution_state
2. Loads any open positions and their orders from database
3. Evaluates exit conditions (SL, TP, signals, time-based) for open positions
4. Evaluates entry signals for new positions
5. Returns order objects (existing SL/TP or new market orders)

By default (persist=True), positions, orders, and trades are saved to the database.
Set persist=False for dry-run evaluation without affecting database state.

Designed for dashboard UIs that render multiple strategy cards.
Fetches all data in batched DB queries (strategies, open position
counts, recent trades) instead of N+1 individual calls.

Score request — exactly one of ``strategies`` / ``runs`` must be set.

The per-request item cap is enforced in the route handler (HTTP 413
on overage); it lives there rather than here so error messages can
cite the actual limit.
SieveScoreRequest.title: SieveScoreRequest

SieveScoreResponse.title: SieveScoreResponse
SieveScoreResponse.description:
Score response.

Probabilities are returned in the same order as the request items.
``model_version`` is a content hash of the bundled artifacts; it changes
when the model is retrained. ``code_version`` is the standard Oracle
provenance stamp (``oracle:<ref> ai:<ref> kb:<ref> roots:<ref>``).

SievePrediction.title: SievePrediction
SievePrediction.description:
Probabilities for one input item.

``binary`` is the go/no-go head: ``{"p_no_trades", "p_trades"}``.
``four_class`` is the outcome head: ``{"losing", "no_trades", "wash",
"winning"}``. Each dict sums to 1.0 within float32 tolerance.

Raw run shape consumed by the SIEVE predictor.

``predict_batch``. Use this when scoring rows already extracted from
the Parquet corpus.
